subject.title: Feature: groupScope option to consolidate group sessions into main

question: Should OpenClaw accept a `groupScope`-style core config for folding selected group/channel peers into the agent main session, and what security/audit/proof gate is required before the linked implementation can land?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the requested config changes transcript/session trust boundaries and adds core routing surface, so maintainer product and security intent is needed before implementation is treated as ready.

options.title: Land after parity and security gates
options.body: Proceed with the linked groupScope direction only after the PR is refreshed, real behavior proof is attached, inbound/outbound behavior is parity-supported, and audit/docs warning posture is settled.

options.title: Narrow to binding-only or named sessions
options.body: Reject a broad global group-to-main default for now and sponsor a narrower per-binding or named shared-session design that limits accidental trust-boundary collapse.

options.title: Defer to broader shared-session design
options.body: Keep this issue open as focused context while maintainers design the broader shared-session contract in the related trackers.

recommendation.title: Land after parity and security gates
recommendation.body: Proceed with the linked groupScope direction only after the PR is refreshed, real behavior proof is attached, inbound/outbound behavior is parity-supported, and audit/docs warning posture is settled.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest visible history across routing, docs, and security-audit boundaries relevant to this decision.
